items.prompt: One representation is shown: 3 shelves with 10 books standing on each shelf. Four equations are listed. Select every equation that correctly matches this representation, and leave unselected any that does not. For each one you select, be ready to say what each factor refers to.

correctAnswer.referentNote: In 3 x 10 the 3 counts the shelves and the 10 counts the books on each shelf. In 10 x 3 the numbers are read in the other order, so 10 counts books in each shelf-group and 3 counts the shelves; the total is the same 30 books either way. The order changes what each factor is read as standing for, not the product.
correctAnswer.verification: Directly countable: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 books shown on the three shelves.

responseContract.inputMode: tap or click to toggle each equation on or off, then one tap to commit; toggles are large, keyboard-free, and hover-free
responseContract.validation: Partial selections are not auto-completed. Feedback addresses each equation the learner judged, affirming both valid orderings and never affirming 3 + 10 = 13 or 10 x 10 = 100 as a match. No formal property name is required or used.
responseContract.incorrectPath: Reasoning retry: the shelves stay on screen and the learner re-checks one equation at a time against the countable books, then re-commits. Progress preserved.
responseContract.hintPolicy: on request only, stepwise: (1) count the total books directly; (2) ask whether each equation's numbers describe groups and amount per group here; (3) check whether the equation's total equals your count. Hint never lists the answer set.

items.academicTarget: Restate the full multiplicative chain — situation to groups and amount per group, to representation, to equation, to verified product — and state what each factor referred to in the learner's own completed work.

supportProgression: Opening orientation (item-01): maximum support. Both governing quantities are offered as bounded choices, no product is demanded, no scoring and no failure state exists. Support here is structural rather than requested — it establishes vocabulary, not performance.

Segment 1 (item-02): high support. Representation and matching equation are both supplied; the learner owns only the product. Stepwise hints become available but are surfaced as an offer the learner may take, never auto-pushed. Hint tier 1 identifies one group, tier 2 counts the groups, tier 3 prompts repeated addition; no tier ever states the product.

Segment 2 (item-03): medium support. The equation is withdrawn — the learner supplies both factors with referents before any equation is revealed. Array language is introduced with the representation still fully given, so exactly one new demand is added at a time. Hints remain on request only and stepwise.

Segment 3 (item-04): low support and the responsibility-transfer point. The representation itself is withdrawn; the learner builds it. The system holds structural integrity (equal groups stay equal, rows stay uniform) but never auto-arranges, never auto-fills a factor, and never reveals the equation before the learner commits. Both an array and an equal-groups build are accepted, so no single structure is presented as the only valid model.

Segment 4 (item-05): low support with judgment shifted entirely to the learner. The representation returns as a reference surface, but the correctness of each candidate equation is the learner's decision, including two valid factor orderings. Hints direct attention to counting and checking, never to the answer set.

Segment 5 (item-06): minimal support, entered only by learner election. Multi-step reasoning with the largest factors; nothing is pushed at any point. Hints exist but must be requested, and stage two cannot be unlocked by the system answering stage one. The learner may exit back to the standard tier without losing progress.

Payoff (item-07): support returns only as retrieval assistance anchored to the learner's own saved work. No new mathematics, unlimited re-answers, and no failure exit — the experience always reaches its close.

Across all segments: every incorrect response routes to a reasoning retry that preserves progress rather than terminating the item. Retries re-expose the countable representation and ask the learner to re-decide, never supplying the decision. Scaffold density decreases monotonically from item-01 through item-06 while learner-constructed content increases; no item repeats within the packet.
input.charterConcern: Two open concerns, both flagged rather than resolved here. First, the responsibility-transfer point is fixed at item-04 by charter progression, but asm-05 is only 0.6 confidence and no supplied evidence addresses construction versus interpretation in mathematics at all. If the construct-vs-read accuracy delta at item-04 proves large, the transfer likely needs an intermediate rung — a partially pre-built representation the learner completes — which this packet does not currently contain and which would require a sixth instructional item. Second, and more structurally: the charter directs a monotonically rising ramp with an optional escalation (asm-02, 0.65 confidence) on the strength of a learner requesting harder riddles. That is verbal-puzzle evidence, and the charter itself names the risk that in mathematics difficulty can read as failure rather than invitation. I have written item-06 as strictly elective with a preserved-progress exit, but I want to note that the escalation offer's framing is a downstream creative decision I do not control, and a competitively framed offer could plausibly discourage rather than motivate. Relatedly, the wrestling-loss evidence underwriting asm-06 (0.5 confidence) establishes only comfort discussing a competitive loss, not any in-task failure response; the retry design should be treated as an untested hypothesis, not a settled accommodation. I have also kept item-05's referent note informal per the out-of-scope rule against formal property names, but describing 10 x 3 as counting shelf-groups of books requires careful downstream wording to stay unambiguous — this is exactly the kind of phrasing asm-04 warns carries trust cost if it lands loosely.
